name: n4_read_history
description: Read the last records of one history, newest first, to prove records arrive (a {ok} history extension proves it runs, not that records exist). Name the history by history_id (/<station>/<history name>, as historyConfig.id shows it) or by ext_ord (the history extension's ORD, e.g. station:|slot:/Folder/Point/NumericInterval, resolved to its id with one BQL select); give exactly one. Each row is {timestamp, value, status} as the station renders them (localized display text, e.g. '15 nov 2026 20:09:35 CST', '21,0', '{ok}'); columns are the station's headers. Optional range: period (today, last24Hours, yesterday, weekToDate, lastWeek, last7Days, monthToDate, lastMonth, yearToDate, lastYear) or start and/or end (BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T00:00:00.000-06:00), not both. truncated is true when the range holds more records than limit; total_records is the range's record count (select count(*)), null with total_records_note when that count failed. A history that cannot be read is an error naming the id and how to list the ids. Read-only: fixed queries over a history: ORD, no file output.

period.description: Period id: today, last24Hours, yesterday, weekToDate, lastWeek, last7Days, monthToDate, lastMonth, yearToDate or lastYear

end.description: Range end as a BAbsTime, e.g. 2026-11-15T23:59:59.999-06:00

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds
